title: Quarterly Relationship Plan — QBR Agenda & Prep Kit
content:
Purpose and positioning:
This is a lightweight, reusable QBR agenda + facilitation script + pre-meeting checklist focused on driving renewals by aligning product value to the customer’s strategic priorities. Use as the single source for the customer-facing meeting and the internal prep. Keep the agenda tight (60–75 minutes) and surface a clear renewal / next-step ask at the end.

Meeting objectives (pick 2–3 per customer):
- Validate strategic/business outcomes achieved since last QBR
- Surface blockers and agree actions to remove adoption friction
- Reconfirm roadmap alignment + co-investment opportunities
- Surface signal(s) that indicate renewal health and next-step cadence

Suggested 65-minute agenda (timeboxes):
1) 0:00–0:05 — Welcome & framing (CS lead)
   - Quick hello, confirm attendees and roles, state top objective for the session.
   - Script line: "Today we're here to review outcomes since last quarter, align on priorities for the next 90 days, and confirm a plan that supports your upcoming renewal decision."

2) 0:05–0:18 — Highlight reel: wins + metrics (Product/CS)
   - 8–10 minute data-backed showcase of 2–3 wins tied to KPIs (ARR impact, time saved, performance gains).
   - Bring: usage trend charts, latency/cost per inference trends, top queries list, NPS/CSAT change.
   - Script line: "Here are the concrete ways Redwood Inference moved the needle for your team — quick examples and the numbers behind them."

3) 0:18–0:35 — Health check & adoption deep-dive (Customer + CS)
   - Walk through adoption segments: key teams, most/least active routes, error trends, cost hot spots.
   - Use open questions: "Which of these initiatives are highest priority for you next quarter?"
   - Runbook note: if usage drops >20% in a critical route, escalate to Solutions Eng for short audit.

4) 0:35–0:50 — Roadmap alignment & opportunities (Product + Customer)
   - Share 2 relevant roadmap items and how they reduce customer's blockers.
   - Co-invest option: propose pilot, dedicated capacity window, or trial of Optimize features.
   - Script line: "If we delivered X by Q2, would that unlock the next project for your org?"

5) 0:50–0:60 — Renewal signals & risk conversation (CS lead)
   - Present renewal signals summary (see signals list below). Call out any open procurement timelines.
   - Script line for strong signal: "Based on the data and your priorities, we'd like to propose a renewal plan that preserves these performance and cost targets."
   - Script line for at-risk: "We hear concerns about X — can we agree a 30/60 day plan to validate fixes and reduce risk before renewal?"

6) 0:60–0:65 — Next steps & close (CS lead + AE)
   - Clear ask: propose renewal window, pricing/discount approach, and 2 immediate actions (technical audit, contract draft).
   - Confirm owners and dates, schedule follow-up check-in.

Facilitation notes & micro-scripts (use adaptable phrasing):
- Opening (30s): "Thanks everyone — quick roll call then I’ll hand to Product for the wins."
- Re-centering (when discussion drifts): "Helpful topic — can we park that and come back after we finish the adoption review?"
- Eliciting commitments: "On a scale of 1–5 how confident are you that this will be in scope next quarter?"
- Handling objections: "I appreciate that. What would you need to see to move this to green?"
- Closing the renewal ask: "To preserve current pricing and guaranteed capacity, we recommend confirming by [X date]. Would you be comfortable moving forward on that timeline?"

Pre-meeting checklist (owner and timings):
- 10 business days out (CS lead): confirm date with customer, share agenda draft, confirm stakeholders.
- 7 business days out (CS lead + AE): collect required artifacts: usage exports, NPS/CSAT, latency/cost report, open-support-tickets list.
- 5 business days out (Product/SE): prepare 2–3 brief slides: metrics, RCA for top error, roadmap items with impact bullets.
- 3 business days out (CS lead): run internal dry-run (15 min) with AE and SE, align on ask and negotiation boundaries.
- 1 business day out (CS lead): share final slide deck and the 2-minute pre-read with customer. Add calendar invite with roles.

Renewal signal checklist (quick scan on QBR) — binary cues + suggested play:
- Topline usage trend: sustained +10% QoQ on core route => signal: supportive (ask for expansion + discuss commit)
- Seat/team growth: active seats rising => signal: supportive (propose tiered pricing pilot)
- Persistent latency/cost spike on heavy inference routes => signal: at-risk for performance/ROI (trigger Solutions Eng audit + cost optimization play)
- Increasing support tickets for accuracy/regression => signal: product risk (start focused evals and regression triage)
- Procurement chatter / legal delays beyond 30 days => signal: timeline risk (AE escalate to deal desk and request fast-track terms)
- Low executive engagement (no execs on invite & low usage) => signal: relationship risk (CS lead request exec intro + strategic workshop)

Risk triage path (if at-risk):
- Triage within 48 hours: CS lead opens "QBR follow-up" ticket and tags Solutions Eng + Product.
- 5 business days: present remediation plan to customer (SLA for fixes, trial of config change, or temp burst capacity).
- 10 business days: check milestone; if unresolved, AE escalation to sales leadership + discuss short-term concessions.

Internal roles & who to loop:
- CS lead: primary facilitator, owner of agenda and follow-up
- AE: commercial ask, discount negotiation, procurement interface
- Solutions Engineer: technical health, errors, optimization play
- Product PM: roadmap tie-ins, feature ask intake
- Customer Exec Sponsor: invited where strategic alignment or renewal > $250k

Post-meeting follow-up templates (short & actionable):
- Follow-up subject: "QBR recap + agreed next steps — [Customer] / [Date]"
- Follow-up body (short): "Thanks for the time today — attached are the notes and the 3 actions we agreed: 1) SE audit due [date] (owner), 2) contract draft by [date] (AE), 3) exec intro scheduled [date] (CS). If any item is off, flag here and we'll adjust. — Aisha"

Reusable artifacts to attach to QBR invite or post-meeting:
- One-page outcome dashboard (usage, latency, cost, support trend, NPS)
- 90-day joint success plan (owners, milestones, measurable outcomes)
- Renewal timeline and decision checkpoints (dates + owners)

Notes on tone and governance:
- Keep the conversation customer-led; use data to guide, not to lecture.
- Avoid surprise commercial asks; coordinate with AE before the meeting if likely to propose pricing changes.
- Maintain a single source of truth — update the joint success plan in the shared Confluence page within 48 hours.

Quick checklist for the meeting pack (to attach):
- 1 slide: Key outcomes & ask
- 1 slide: Top 3 metrics (usage, latency, cost) with short blurb
- 1 slide: Roadmap items mapped to customer blockers
- 1 appendix: Open tickets + action owner table

Open questions / friction points we still need to decide (internal):
- Standard language for small concession offers to de-risk renewals (who signs off?).
- When to proactively offer a limited dedicated capacity pilot vs. recommend Optimize tweaks.
- Acceptance criteria for marking a renewal as "green" in our trackers.

Revision history: 
- v0.1 (2025-11-20) initial draft — Aisha
- v0.2 (2026-01-12) added risk triage flow and pre-meeting timeline — Lucas
- v0.3 (2026-02-25) polished facilitation scripts and included post-meeting templates — Mei

Use this doc as the fast-start for customer-specific QBRs. Copy into the customer folder, drop the data artifacts, and replace the scripted lines with customer names/org-specific phrasing before the meeting.
